title: Work IQ: policy-based governance of agents and their capabilities
summary: The roadmap facts, administrative paths and commands are supported, including the server-blocking path in the updated access-control guide. Two descriptive claims remain unconfirmed: that policy consists of a single switch and that the access-control guide is preview documentation. The mutation-default statement also needs to acknowledge Microsoft's different wording for Copilot Studio.

claims.quote: Provide administrators with policy-based controls for governing agents and their capabilities at scale.

claims.claim: The item lists Work IQ and Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365).
claims.quote: "products": ["Work IQ", "Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365)"]

claims.quote: The policy layer uses Rego, the policy language from Open Policy Agent (OPA), to express authorization rules.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: MCP policy can restrict requested resource paths at request time.
claims.quote: It adds a request-time governance layer that can allow or deny specific MCP tool requests based on tenant policy.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: MCP policy can restrict operations and capabilities used by agents.
claims.quote: For example, a tenant policy can allow read access to common productivity data while blocking high-risk paths, write operations, or large collection traversal.

claims.claim: MCP policy can govern data retrieval.
claims.quote: Data retrieval limits | Whether collection reads are bounded to reduce large-scale data extraction risk

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; controls[0]
claims.claim: Learn documents an initial tenant-level Work IQ MCP policy on/off control in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: In the initial release, Work IQ MCP provides tenant-level policy control. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, tenant administrators can turn Work IQ MCP policy on or off for the tenant.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The MCP policy guide says mutation operations, including create, update, delete and sending email, are disallowed by default.
claims.quote: By default, mutation operations aren't allowed for safety. This restriction includes create, update, delete, and action requests that modify data, such as sending email.
claims.fix: Keep the attribution to the MCP policy guide and add: 'The Copilot Studio Work IQ guide separately says write operations are on by default, subject to organizational permissions and policies; check the applicable experience rather than assuming a uniform write default.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/add-work-iq#work-iq-key-features, which says 'Write operations are on by default. Your organization's permissions and policies still apply.'

claims.claim: Administrators can enable supported mutation scenarios through tenant policy.
claims.quote: Administrators can enable supported mutation scenarios through tenant policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center when those capabilities are needed.

claims.claim: The cited MCP policy guide does not link itself to roadmap item 570652.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "policy" "retroactive" "570652". Opened Policy governance for Work IQ MCP in full; it contains no roadmap number or link identifying this item.

claims.where: What's changing: final paragraph; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap item's scope beyond documented MCP controls and its relationship to Agent 365 lifecycle governance remain unconfirmed.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "policy" "retroactive" "570652". Read the roadmap record and MCP policy guide; results describe MCP request policy, not additional scope or lifecycle rules for this roadmap item.

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: A separate licensing model for this governance control has not yet been published.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "policy" "default" "licensing"; "Work IQ MCP" "policy governance" "licence" "price". Read MCP policy governance, Enable your tenant for Work IQ, and Plan licensing and cost; none names a separate governance-control licence.

claims.claim: No separate price or meter for this governance control is published.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ MCP" "policy governance" "licence" "price". Read MCP policy governance and Plan licensing and cost; API consumption is documented, but no separate governance-control price or meter is specified.

claims.claim: The roadmap item names no licence, add-on or meter.
claims.quote: "description": "Provide administrators with policy-based controls for governing agents and their capabilities at scale."

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance controls: final paragraph; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Work IQ API use is separately metered through consumption-based billing in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: You pay for use of the Work IQ API through a consumption-based model that uses Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: The tenant policy path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Agents > Tools. ... In the tools registry, select Work IQ MCP. ... On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.claim: An API or automation call for the tenant policy on/off control is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ MCP" "policy" "API" "PowerShell". Read MCP policy governance in full and search results for MCP overview and tool reference; none supplies an administrative on/off endpoint or command.

claims.claim: The server-blocking path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Block.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools. ... Select Work IQ MCP. ... To block access to the server, select Block.

claims.claim: An API or automation call to block the Work IQ MCP server is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ MCP" "Block" "API" "PowerShell". Read Manage AI experience access and results for MCP migration, overview and tool reference; no administrative server-blocking call was documented.

claims.claim: No admin-center configuration path is documented for creating the Work IQ service principal.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "enable" "service principal" "admin center". Read Enable your tenant for Work IQ and Foundry setup; the Admin center tab directs readers to a POST in Graph Explorer, not an admin-center configuration path.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/servicePrincipals with appId fdcc1f02-fc51-4226-8753-f668596af7f7 provisions the Work IQ resource for the organization.
claims.quote: Set the method to POST and the URL to https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals. ... { "appId": "fdcc1f02-fc51-4226-8753-f668596af7f7" }

claims.claim: The service principal can alternatively be created with az ad sp create --id <appId>.
claims.quote: Create the Work IQ service principal in your organization by running the following command. ... az ad sp create --id fdcc1f02-fc51-4226-8753-f668596af7f7

claims.claim: Grant or revoke consent in Entra ID > App registrations > app > API permissions, using Grant admin consent for [your tenant] or WorkIQAgent.Ask > Revoke admin consent respectively.
claims.quote: go to Entra ID > App registrations > select the app > API permissions. Select Grant admin consent for [your tenant]. ... On the same API permissions page, select the WorkIQAgent.Ask permission and select Revoke admin consent.

claims.where: controls[3].api; Governance controls table; following paragraph
claims.claim: az ad app permission admin-consent --id <appId> grants consent for the registered application.
claims.quote: Add the WorkIQAgent.Ask delegated permission and grant consent. ... az ad app permission admin-consent --id $APP_ID

claims.claim: The quickstart adds the requested WorkIQAgent.Ask permission with az ad app permission add before running admin-consent.
claims.quote:
az ad app permission add --id $APP_ID \
  --api fdcc1f02-fc51-4226-8753-f668596af7f7 \
  --api-permissions "0b1715fd-f4bf-4c63-b16d-5be31f9847c2=Scope"
az ad app permission admin-consent --id $APP_ID

claims.claim: Admin consent provides per-application control over access to Work IQ on behalf of users.
claims.quote: As an Entra admin, you control which applications in your tenant can access Work IQ data on behalf of users.

claims.where: Governance controls: first paragraph after table

claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ MCP" "policy" "API" "PowerShell". Read MCP policy governance in full; it documents on/off, supported mutation configuration and toggle-style and numeric settings, but does not say the layer consists of one switch.
claims.fix: Replace 'In the initial release the policy layer is a single tenant-level switch' with 'In the initial release, Work IQ MCP policy control is tenant-level'.

claims.where: Governance controls: first paragraph after table
claims.claim: More granular policy controls and templates are described as possible later additions.
claims.quote: More granular controls and policy templates might be added later based on customer requests, feedback, and usage.

claims.claim: Spending policies can include or exclude Work IQ API.
claims.quote: Include Cowork and exclude Work IQ API from a policy when its users shouldn't consume credits through Work IQ API.

claims.claim: Spending policies can set spending limits.
claims.quote: Set policy and per-user limits | Limit monthly consumption for selected user groups and the services covered by their policies.

claims.claim: Spending policies do not reserve credits for a workload, user or group.
claims.quote: Spending policies control access and spending limits; they don't reserve or allocate credits for a workload, user, or group.

claims.claim: Whether the new governance control starts enforcing on arrival is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ MCP" "policy" "on by default" "off by default". Read roadmap, MCP policy governance and search results; mutation defaults are stated, but the control's initial on/off state is not.

claims.claim: The linked Copilot Credits spending-policy guide provides general billing setup.
claims.quote: Use the Cost Management dashboard in the Microsoft 365 admin center to enable usage-based billing, activate the default spending policy, create identity-based and resource-based spending policies.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; sources

Keep the AI Administrator requirement unchanged.
